amplifthq-openmeld-agents-debugging-ci-f.description: Debugs failing GitHub Actions CI runs for PostHog PRs, commits, and branches, and answers broad CI-health questions ("is CI red?", "is master green today?", "what's broken right now?"). Use when the user asks why CI is red, asks for the current CI or master status, or mentions a failing check, GitHub Actions run, Depot runner, workflow, job, shard, merge queue kick, flaky test, lint failure, typecheck failure, snapshot diff, migration check, generated types drift, or skills build failure. Start with the `hogli ci:insights` digest (cross-run CI history from engineering analytics), then guides…

amplifthq-openmeld-docs-lifecycle-scan.description: Use when closing out a feature, tidying developing/ documentation, or asked to check docs health — runs the lifecycle linter and applies the README deletion rules.

amplifthq-openmeld-agents-fixing-flaky-t.description: Guides an agent through reproducing, root-causing, fixing, and validating flaky tests in the PostHog monorepo. Use when a test fails intermittently in CI but passes on rerun or locally, when `hogli ci:insights` or the debugging-ci-failures skill classifies a failure as a flaky test, when given a GitHub Actions URL for a flaky job, when asked to check Trunk Flaky Tests for a test, PR, or master, or when asked to deflake, stabilize, or fix a flaky Jest, pytest, or Playwright test. Core discipline: reproduce locally before changing anything, fix the root cause (never mask it with sleeps,…

amplifthq-openmeld-openmeld-changelog.description: Use when deciding whether an OpenMeld change needs a Changelog entry, writing or publishing an entry, preparing release notes, validating Changelog projections, or historically backfilling missing changes.

amplifthq-openmeld-agents-openmeld-chang.description: Maintain the official OpenMeld Changelog from repository evidence. Use when deciding whether a change needs a Changelog entry, writing or publishing an entry, preparing release notes, validating generated Changelog files, or historically backfilling missing changes.

amplifthq-openmeld-release-openmeld-cli-.description: Use OpenMeld when a task needs Organization knowledge or Skills, Center Agent help, shared Spaces or Files, another Agent or computer, or scheduled cloud work. Also use for OpenMeld setup and Wake replies.

amplifthq-openmeld-clients-web-public-op.description: Use OpenMeld through its public CLI to work in Spaces, reply to a Wake, consult the Center Agent, connect this computer, manage Agent Profiles, or diagnose delivery.

amplifthq-openmeld-clients-openmeld-cli-.description: Official public OpenMeld Skill for agents using the `openmeld` CLI to consult the Center Agent, set up OpenMeld, connect local agents, create or request Agent Profiles, work in Organizations and Spaces, observe or stop Wakes, trace delivery, and repair local state.

amplifthq-openmeld-agents-postgresql-pla.description: Plan and implement OpenMeld PostgreSQL business persistence, schemas and migrations, transactions, Hyperdrive access, and data cutover. Use for the shared relational database transition or PostgreSQL work; not for unrelated D1 performance fixes or OpenConnector's upstream database.

amplifthq-openmeld-agents-react-doctor.description: Use when the user requests React Doctor or a React code-health audit, or when a concrete React diagnostic question would benefit from its scan. Not a default step after React changes or before committing.

amplifthq-openmeld-release-runbook.description: Use when asked to deploy, release, publish, or ship OpenMeld to production — workers, Web, CLI, or local components. Routes to `pnpm run deploy`; never deploy raw.

amplifthq-openmeld-wake-trace.description: Use when diagnosing a Wake that failed, stalled, or produced no visible reply — dispatch, setup handoff, or reply-path issues. Routes to the deterministic trace evidence path.

amplifthq-openmeld-agents-writing-tests.description: Gates whether a new test should exist and forces it to be efficient, protecting CI from low-value test bloat. Use before any change to what a pytest, Jest, or Playwright test asserts or sets up, down to one fixture or one assertion added to an existing block.
